questions.q: What core assumption do sequence models drop compared to the models used earlier in the course?
options: That the target variable must be continuous
That each row of data can be treated as an independent example, unrelated to its ordering
That features must be normalized before training
That the dataset must contain more than one asset
questions.explain: Sequence models learn from an ordered window of history rather than treating each row as an independent snapshot, which is the key shift from the earlier tabular approaches.

questions.q: What problem do LSTMs and GRUs solve relative to plain RNNs?
options: They eliminate the need for any training data
They remove the need for a loss function
They use gating mechanisms to better carry information across longer sequences, addressing the vanishing-gradient problem
They convert the sequence into a single static feature
questions.explain: Plain RNNs struggle to retain information over long sequences. LSTMs and GRUs add gates that let the network learn what to keep, update, or forget, making longer lookback windows practical.

questions.q: What mechanism do Transformers use instead of strict step-by-step recurrence?
options: Random feature shuffling
Attention, which weighs the relevance of every position in the sequence directly
A fixed sliding average
Manual feature engineering only
questions.explain: Transformers replace recurrence with attention, letting the model directly weigh how relevant every other position in the sequence is, which avoids vanishing gradients and parallelizes better.

questions.q: Why do sequence models compound the leakage risks discussed in Chapter 4?
options: Because sequence models never use held-out test data
Because consecutive training windows overlap heavily (e.g., 19 of 20 days for a daily-stepped 20-day window), extending the overlapping-outcomes problem to every input window
Because sequence models cannot be validated at all
Because Transformers do not support cross-validation
questions.explain: If a sequence window is stepped forward one day at a time, consecutive training examples share almost all of their input window, which is the same overlapping-outcomes leakage problem from Chapter 1 and Chapter 4, now baked into the input construction itself.

questions.q: According to the lesson, where do sequence models most legitimately earn their place in quant finance?
options: As a default replacement for all tree-based and linear models
Only for annual financial statement analysis
Short-horizon microstructure (e.g., order-book dynamics) or high-frequency settings with enough data to support a large model
Exclusively for predicting GDP growth
questions.explain: Given their added complexity, overfitting risk, and the leakage concerns around overlapping windows, sequence models are best justified for short-horizon microstructure problems or high-frequency data where there's genuinely enough data to support them.
